questions.topic: translation of nested universal quantifiers, material implication, and distinctness
questions.solutionIndependentCheck: The Persian sentence requires forall x: (boy(x) and likes(x,Maryam)) -> forall y: (boy(y) and likes(Maryam,y) and y != x) -> dislikes(x,y). Option 4 alone includes the outer implication, inner implication, and the distinctness guard. Option 3 omits distinctness; options 1 and 2 misplace conjunction/implication or y scope.

questions.topic: canonical conjunctive normal form from a partial truth table
questions.solutionIndependentCheck: The four shown true rows are 111,110,101,011. The four remaining rows 000,001,010,100 yield the four maxterms (p or q or r), (p or q or not r), (p or not q or r), (not p or q or r), exactly option 2.

questions.topic: validity of syllogisms with universal and existential premises
questions.solutionIndependentCheck: An ignorant human exists. Since every human is a thinker, that witness is an ignorant thinker. In (b), a one-person model with a human who is both ignorant and a thinker satisfies both premises, but refutes the conclusion that no human is ignorant.
